newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. recommends renewal of its Tajikistan mission.
newsitem.headline: U.N. recommends renewal of its Tajikistan mission.

text.p: Secretary-General Kofi Annan recommended on Wednesday a three-month renewal of a small U.N. observer mission in civil war-torn Tajikistan and said he would later propose boosting its strength and mandate.
The U.N. Mission of Observers in Tajikistan (UNMOT) comprises 22 military observers, out of an authorised strength of 45, and some 50 civilian personnel. Its current mandate expires June 15.

UNMOT works with a large force of Russian-led troops deployed by the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS) as border guards and internal peacekeepers in the mountainous country bordering Afghanistan and China.
Tens of thousands of people have died and many more have lost their homes in fighting which has devastated the former Soviet republic since it gained independence in 1991.

In a written report to the Security Council, Annan said an accord signed in Tehran on May 28 by the Tajik government and the United Tajik Opposition (UTO) completed a series of agreements between the parties.
But he said the tasks they assigned to UNMOT were not fully covered by its present mandate, nor did UNMOT have the present capacity to perform them.
Stressing the importance of security, Annan said in certain parts of Tajikistan the deployment of unarmed personnel entailed an unacceptable level risk and they would therefore need to be protected.
One possibility would be for the CIS force to assume that responsibility, provided all parties concurred.

"I intend to revert to the Security Council with recommendations concerning the adjustment of the UNMOT mandate and strength once answers have been found to this and other open questions that will require decisions by the Commission on National Reconciliation," he said, referring to the body that will be responsible for implementing the accords until elections are held.

A spokesman for Tajiki President Imomali Rakhmonov said on Tuesday that the planned signing of a final peace accord in Moscow on June 14 had been postponed until later in the month "for technical reasons."
On Wednesday the U.N. special representative in Tajikistan, Gerd Dietrich Merrem, expressed concern about a build-up of government and opposition forces near Dushanbe, the capital.
